messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: service=runtime-canary region=eu-west-1 severity=high — 5xx spike detected for canary users. page: @oncall (Alex) 2355002468

Alex: on it — seeing canary error rate jump to ~12% in eu-west-1. correlating with last deploy (pipeline 2026-03-15T01:05Z).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout failed: image manifest signature mismatch for image redwood/runtime:2026-03-15-canary (expected digest sha256:abcd..., got sha256:xxxx...).

Maya: @Alex any recent CI changes? I just ran the quick-build job and got a different manifest id locally.

Alex: pipeline logs show `gcr.io/ci/artifact-sign` step succeeded but `registry` returned 202 Accepted and then a 500 on final manifest finalize. suspect remote registry returned transient 5xx but left a dangling tag -> canary pulling inconsistent manifest.

Cheng: digging into canary hosts logs — lots of `manifest unknown` and `unexpected EOF` from docker pull. sample log: ```
Mar 15 01:06:12 canary-node kubelet[1234]: E03015 01:06:12.345 Pulling image "gcr.io/redwood/runtime:2026-03-15-canary"
Mar 15 01:06:13 canary-node containerd: failed to resolve reference: failed to query registry: MANIFEST_UNKNOWN
```

Sasha: Customer impact? any external errors surfaced in Sentry/Prod?

Maya: A small subset of requests routed to canary return 500s; front door retries escalate errors. Traffic split was 5% canary — we're seeing ~0.6% of total requests with errors, concentrated in eu-west. Not global outage but visible to some customers.

Alex: action plan: 1) Pause canary traffic / flip feature flag kill-switch, 2) rollback canary to previous stable image, 3) investigate registry finalize step/CI signature.

Sasha: +1. Who can flip the flag now? I can.

Alex: Sasha please toggle `runtime_canary_enabled` -> false for eu-west. Also open kill switch in rollout config: `kubectl -n runtime set image deployment/runtime runtime=gcr.io/redwood/runtime:stable-2026-03-08` is fallback but prefer flag first.

Sasha: done. `feature-flag runtime_canary_enabled = false` -> confirmed. Notifying routing. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Traffic routing updated: canary traffic -> 0%.

Cheng: starting rollback of canary pods to stable image to clear any cached bad manifests: `kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deployment/runtime --to-image=gcr.io/redwood/runtime:stable-2026-03-08`

Alex: hold on, before rolling back ensure we don't have in-cluster image cache still pointing to dangling tag. Cheng, run `crictl images | grep 2026-03-15-canary` on nodes and purge if present.

Cheng: did purge on eu-west nodes. removed dangling layers.

Maya: confirming Sentry spikes stopped after flag flip. error rate down to baseline in ~2m. Looks like kill-switch worked.

Alex: good. Now we need to block the bad tag from being reused. I’ll open a registry block request and set the affected tag to immutable/frozen until we understand root cause.

Sasha: Also paging ENG-SEC for potential registry auth/signing issues? it might be a signing race. @Cheng can you capture the pipeline artifact metadata and signature outputs: `gsutil cat gs://ci-artifacts/runtime/2026-03-15-canary/*.sig`

Cheng: grabbed signatures and manifest medata, pushing to #eng-infra-private. snippet: ```
manifest: {"schemaVersion":2, "mediaType":"application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json", "config":{"digest":"sha256:abcd..."}}
signature: vac-sign-2026-03-15 signer=ci-builder id=ci-37
registry-response: 202 Accepted -> later 500 during finalize (tx 0x5fa3)
```

Alex: preliminary hypothesis: CI pushed manifest then registry returned 202 pending, followed by 500 during finalization leaving a partially-written manifest and a tag bound to inconsistent digest. Pullers could see either digest depending on timing. That explains intermittent MANIFEST_UNKNOWN.

Sasha: Customer impact note for CSMs: "Partial canary deployment caused a small percentage of requests in eu-west to 500. No data loss, traffic rolled back. Affected customers: subset on canary routing — we will follow up if needed."

Bob: I'm on handoff in 30m — want to do an on-call swap? my pager's free after 02:00Z.

Alex: I'll stay on until rollback confirmed and registry blocked. Sasha can take next-hand. Bob, if you can take subsequent 4h that'd be great.

Bob: taking handoff at 02:00Z. leaving a short runbook note: `If manifest mismatch on registry: 1) flip feature flag; 2) set canary=0; 3) purge node caches; 4) rollback canary; 5) block tag in registry; 6) collect signatures & pipeline logs`

Maya: postmortem action items: create ticket INFRA-REG-2026, add CI retry/finalize safeguards, add a registry healthcheck before finalize, and mark the pipeline step as non-idempotent — add robust rollback.

Alex: agreed. Also add Canary gating: do not route traffic until registry finalize returns stable 200 and digest verify succeeds from at least 2 registry replicas.

Sasha: closing the page — monitoring for 15m. if error resurfaces we reopen. :eyes:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated — page closed by Alex at 2355003240. Please file followup and label severity=medium, cause=registry-finalize-failure, impact=partial-canary-5xx-0.6% total requests.

Cheng: saved collected artifacts in gs://redwood/incident/2355002468/, including pipeline traces, registry responses, host logs.

Alex: thanks everyone. follow-up owners: Maya (postmortem), Cheng (artifact investigation), Sasha (registry block + gating), Bob (oncall_watch).

Sasha: noted — will create the incident ticket and ping CSMs with templated customer message.

Bob: handed off. good job. :thumbsup:
